extracted.intended_audience: people who review workplace or academic writing (colleagues, peer reviewers, mentors)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical pointers for colleagues doing peer review of workplace or academic drafts, focusing on constructive, efficient, and reader-centered feedback. Emphasizes process (timing, scope) and tone (truthful but sensitive) as well as organization of comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the writer's goals and intended reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Find out what the writer is trying to accomplish and who the reader is before commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the document's purpose and audience first so your comments are aligned to the author's objectives rather than your assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the whole piece first
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the entire piece before giving advice — questions might be answered later in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid premature judgement; some issues resolve later in the text. A full read prevents wasted or conflicting suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Get back to your colleague quickly — they may be under deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is part of being helpful; fast feedback enables revision cycles and respects the author's schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest but sensitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the truth, but be sensitive at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance candor with empathy: don't sugarcoat important problems, but deliver criticism in a way that preserves the writer's confidence and receptivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with positives and highlight strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Make initial comments positive and identify the best parts — keeps the review pleasant and gives the colleague a clear example of what's correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with what works to create a constructive tone and to provide concrete models the author can emulate in revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize comments from big to small (inverted pyramid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize comments in an inverted pyramid — start with big issues (effectiveness), then organization, then word choice / grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize high-impact issues (overall effectiveness, argument, structure) before nitpicks so the author can address major problems first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specific examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Give as many specific examples as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to exact passages, suggest precise rewrites or alternatives, and illustrate problems and solutions rather than making vague observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the author what to extend and what to cut
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the writer what to extend and what to cut — keep your peer brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, actionable guidance about where to add development and where to remove material; be concise and focused so the author can act efficiently.
